source.title: MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision
source.authors: I. Tolstikhin; N. Houlsby; Alexander Kolesnikov; Lucas Beyer; Xiao-Hua Zhai; T. Unterthiner; Jessica Yung; A. Steiner; Daniel Keysers; J. Uszkoreit; M. Lučić; A. Dosovitskiy

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports overfitting observations and compares image-classification accuracy across architectures, but does not test the mapped claim versions: it uses no random-label fit test, interpolation-threshold width sweep, fully connected versus convolutional comparison, optimizer or batch comparison, dropout ablation, sharpness measurement, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that Mixer overfits in some settings and performs worse than ViT despite similar training loss. These observations concern generalization but do not measure a mapped version. Its reported regularization settings and comparisons to other model families are not ablations of the mapped claim objects.
record.test_reason: The study measures Mixer accuracy, transfer performance and overfitting, but none of V1–V8 directly. Mixer uses patch-local projections and shared token/channel MLPs; it is not the fully connected architecture specified in V3. Its comparisons with CNNs therefore do not directly test V3. No reported ablation isolates dropout, optimizer or batch-size effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the overfitting observations but omits the main conclusion: Mixer achieves a competitive accuracy–compute trade-off without convolutional or attention layers. Larger datasets substantially improve performance; understanding learned features and their inductive biases remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates an all-MLP vision architecture using large-scale pre-training and transfer learning; it does not reproduce the mapped original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports stronger overfitting for smaller pre-training datasets and differing outcomes across model scales and architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixer overfits more than similarly scaled ViT models on ImageNet; all tested Mixer models strongly overfit on the smallest JFT subset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixer generalization depends on architecture and training-data scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Under global pixel permutation, Mixer loses approximately 45% of its linear 5-shot accuracy versus approximately 75% for ResNet; patch-and-within-patch permutation leaves Mixer performance unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixer and ResNet differ in their dependence on spatial input organization.

record.problems: The overfitting statements are qualitative and lack numeric training loss or train-test gaps. The study uses pre-training and transfer settings that do not directly isolate the mapped claim conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results identified. Benchmark accuracy and throughput comparisons do not measure one of the mapped versions or the generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold; model scaling changes depth and other dimensions without establishing interpolation.
CNN versus fully connected network generalization and the contribution of local connectivity; Mixer has structured connectivity and parameter sharing.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning; pre-training with Adam and fine-tuning with SGD are different stages, not an optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout's effect on held-out error. Dropout rates were searched, but no comparative outcomes are reported; selected rates are zero.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not a rejection of the reported overfitting observations. Table 4's selected dropout rates of zero are selection results, not evidence that dropout fails to improve generalization.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out accuracy comparison.
No one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional networks with fully connected networks trained from scratch.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout is included in some training recipes, but its effect on test error is not reported as an ablation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-gap measure.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

rows.subject: Mixer-B/16
rows.size_stated: Base scale; 59M parameters per Table 1 for B/16 (input resolution 224, classifier head excluded).
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained from random initialization on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained from scratch on ImageNet; compared with ViT-B/16 training curves and downstream accuracy.

conditions.value: extra regularization; details not stated here

rows.measure: ImageNet top-1 accuracy and qualitative train-loss/overfitting comparison
rows.baseline: ViT-B/16 reaches 79.67% ImageNet top-1 accuracy; training losses are described as very similar.
rows.value: 76.44% ImageNet top-1 accuracy; the paper says Mixer-B/16 overfits more than ViT-B/16.
rows.note: The paper does not give numeric training losses or a numeric train-test gap.
rows.check: The accuracy and qualitative overfitting comparison are correct, but measure no listed version. Regularization details are available in Table 4: weight decay 0.1, RandAugment magnitude 15, mixup 0.5, dropout 0.0 and stochastic depth 0.1.

rows.subject: Mixer-L/16
rows.size_stated: Large scale; 207M parameters per Table 1 for L/16 (input resolution 224, classifier head excluded).
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained from random initialization on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared with ViT-L/16 on ImageNet; paper describes an overfitting difference.

conditions.value: extra regularization; details not stated here

rows.value: The paper says the overfitting difference between Mixer-L/16 and ViT-L/16 is even more pronounced than for the base models.
rows.note: No numeric accuracy or training-loss values for this comparison are given in the cited passage.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison is correct but measures no listed version. Numeric accuracies are available in Table 3: Mixer-L/16 reaches 71.76% versus ViT-L/16 at 76.11%, both at resolution 224 after 300 ImageNet training epochs. The note implying these values are unavailable should be corrected.

rows.subject: Mixer models (all models in the reported subset sweep; individual model outcomes not stated in this sentence)
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained on increasing training-set sizes with the same total number of steps; early stopping used based on best upstream validation performance.

conditions.value: smallest subset of JFT-300M; percentage not specified in the result sentence
233, 70, 23, and 7 epochs for 3%, 10%, 30%, and 100% subsets respectively

rows.baseline: BiT models in the same setting, which also overfit but to a lesser extent.
rows.value: The paper states that all Mixer models strongly overfit on the smallest JFT-300M subset.
rows.note: The statement aggregates Mixer models; the paper does not assign separate overfitting values to each model here.
rows.check: The overfitting statement is correct but measures no listed version. The smallest subset is explicitly 3% of JFT-300M, trained for 233 epochs. Figure 2 reports linear 5-shot ImageNet accuracy as a transfer proxy, not a numeric train–test gap.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
